name: Karina Aznavourian
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze medal in women's team épée at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics at age 22.
early_history_summary: Born in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR to an Armenian-Azerbaijani family, Aznavourian moved to Moscow in 1990 at age 16. She switched from foil to épée and trained under coach Alexander Kislyunin, graduating from the Olympic Reserve School No. 3 and the Russian State University of Physical Education before making the Russian national team.
family_context_summary: Born in Baku to an Armenian-Azerbaijani family; relocated to Moscow in 1990, likely due to ethnic tensions surrounding the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Olympic Reserve School, Russian national fencing team, coach Kislyunin, displacement from Baku
evidence_summary: Aznavourian benefited from the Russian Olympic fencing pipeline, training at the specialized Olympic Reserve School No. 3 in Moscow under coach Alexander Kislyunin after relocating from Baku at age 16. Her displacement from Baku likely created urgency to establish herself in Moscow. By 22, she was on the Russian national team winning Olympic bronze in the debut women's team épée event at the 1996 Atlanta Games. Family financial background and parental domain expertise are not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR to an Armenian-Azerbaijani family; moved to Moscow in 1990 at age 16.
current_position: Director of Moscow Olympic Reserve School No. 3 since 2012; retired from competitive fencing in 2008; resides in Russia.

name: Junior dos Santos
milestone_by_age_26: Made a stunning UFC debut at UFC 90 on October 25, 2008, knocking out top heavyweight contender Fabricio Werdum in the first round at age 24.
early_history_summary: Raised by a single mother in Caçador, Santa Catarina, Brazil after his alcoholic father left the family, dos Santos started working at age 10. He trained in capoeira throughout his teenage years before beginning Brazilian jiu-jitsu at 21 under Yuri Carlton. After winning local BJJ tournaments, he added boxing training under Luiz Carlos Dórea and turned professional in MMA in 2006 at age 22, fighting in small Brazilian promotions before being signed by the UFC.

parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family faced significant poverty.

evidence_summary: Dos Santos grew up in extreme poverty in rural Brazil, raised by a single mother after his alcoholic father abandoned the family. He started working at age 10 and trained in capoeira as a teenager before beginning formal martial arts training at 21. His natural heavyweight power and athleticism, combined with training under Yuri Carlton (BJJ) and Luiz Dórea (boxing), and later mentorship from Antonio Rodrigo Nogueira, propelled him to a stunning UFC debut knockout of Fabricio Werdum at age 24. The UFC/MMA boom of the late 2000s provided a structural wave.

name: Bjørg Eva Jensen
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in the 3000m at the 1980 Lake Placid Winter Olympics at age 20, the only gold medal Norway won at those Games.
early_history_summary: Born in Larvik, Norway, Jensen began her international speed skating career at age 15 at the 1976 World Junior Championships. She progressed steadily, winning World Junior bronze in 1977, silver in 1978 and 1979, and gold in 1980. She also placed third at the senior World Allround Championships in 1980, one month before her Olympic gold. She is the only skater to medal in four consecutive World Junior Championships.
family_context_summary: Born in Larvik, Norway; member of local skating club IF Fram. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Norway speed skating tradition, IF Fram Larvik, junior championship progression, Olympic pipeline
evidence_summary: Jensen grew up in Larvik, Norway, a country with a deep speed skating tradition, and trained at the local IF Fram club. She competed internationally from age 15, winning medals at four consecutive World Junior Championships (1977-1980), a unique achievement. The Norwegian skating ecosystem provided elite training infrastructure and competition pathways. Her family background is not documented in reviewed sources. She won Olympic gold at 20 but her results gradually declined afterward as East German and Soviet skaters dominated.
starting_point: Born in Larvik, Norway; member of local skating club IF Fram from a young age.
current_position: Retired from competitive speed skating; lives in Norway; only Norwegian female speed skater to win an Olympic title through 2010.

name: Jin Xing
milestone_by_age_26: Won the highest prize at the first Taoli Cup national dance competition in 1985 at age 18, becoming the first man to dance on pointe in China.
early_history_summary: Born in Shenyang, China to a Chosonjok family, Jin joined the People's Liberation Army at age 9 to train in dance with a military troupe affiliated with the Shenyang Military Region. At 12, she transferred to the PLA Art Academy, graduating with honours in 1984 at age 17. She returned to the Shenyang military dance troupe, attained the rank of colonel, and won the national dance competition in 1985 before moving to New York on a scholarship in 1989.
family_context_summary: Born to a Chosonjok family in Shenyang; mother was a translator and father was a military intelligence officer. Jin joined the PLA at age 9 with parental permission after fasting for two days.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a military intelligence officer and mother was a translator, providing an educated family environment with military connections that facilitated entry into the PLA dance system.
primary_early_advantage_tags: PLA dance troupe, PLA Art Academy, military training from age 9, Taoli Cup, pointe dance pioneer
evidence_summary: Jin Xing's extraordinary early dance career was built on the PLA's institutional pipeline: she entered military dance training at age 9, transferred to the elite PLA Art Academy at 12, and graduated with honours at 17. Her father's military intelligence background may have facilitated entry into the PLA system. She won the highest prize at the first Taoli Cup national dance competition at 18, pioneering pointe work for male dancers in China. The intense, full-immersion military training environment provided 9 years of concentrated practice before her national breakthrough. She later moved to New York on scholarship in 1989.
starting_point: Born in Shenyang, China to a Chosonjok family; father was a military intelligence officer, mother was a translator.
current_position: Chinese TV personality and dancer; founder of Jin Xing Dance Theater Shanghai; visibility curtailed by Chinese government since 2021; age 58 as of 2025.

name: Jānis Lūsis
milestone_by_age_26: Won European Championship gold in javelin throw at the 1962 Belgrade championships at age 23 with a championship record of 82.04m, and followed with Olympic bronze at the 1964 Tokyo Games at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Jelgava, Latvia, Lūsis trained at the Daugava Voluntary Sports Society and later at the Armed Forces sports society within the Soviet athletic system. He won his first Soviet national title in 1962 at age 23, then captured the European Championship gold the same year with a championship record throw, ending the season with a world-leading 86.04m. He went undefeated in 1963 and won the Universiade gold before taking Olympic bronze in 1964.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Trained within the Soviet sports society system.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet sports system, Daugava sports society, Armed Forces sports society, European Championship 1962

He won his first Soviet title and European Championship gold in 1962 at age 23, throwing a championship record of 82.04m and a world-leading 86.04m that season. The Soviet sports system provided full-time training support and elite competition access. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources. He went on to become the greatest javelin thrower in history, named so by IAAF in 1987.
starting_point: Born in Jelgava, Latvia; trained within the Soviet state sports system at Daugava Voluntary Sports Society and Armed Forces sports society.
current_position: Died on April 29, 2020 in Riga, Latvia at age 80; final role: retired athletics coach and official.

name: Anna Hazare

early_history_summary: Born Kisan Baburao Hazare in Bhingar, near Ahmednagar, Bombay Presidency, British India, to an impoverished family. His father worked as an unskilled labourer at an Ayurveda pharmacy. Hazare's schooling ended at the seventh grade. He sold flowers at Dadar railway station in Mumbai and owned two flower shops before being drafted into the Indian Army in April 1960, where he served as a truck driver for 15 years.

His social activism career began after leaving the army, with the transformation of Ralegan Siddhi village in the 1970s and the anti-corruption movement peaking in 2011. name: Nikolai Andrianov
milestone_by_age_26: Won two gold medals (pommel horse, vault) at the 1971 European Championships in Madrid at age 19, followed by Olympic gold in floor exercise at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Vladimir, Russian SFSR, Andrianov was raised by his mother. He entered the Children and Youth Sports School of the Burevestnik sports society at age 11, where he was spotted by renowned coach Nikolai Tolkachev, who became his surrogate father. Selected for the USSR national team at 18, his first international success came at the 1971 European Championships where he won six medals including two golds. He won Olympic gold in floor exercise at the 1972 Munich Games at age 20.
family_context_summary: Raised by his mother in Vladimir, approximately 190km east of Moscow. Family financial background not documented; Tolkachev served as a surrogate father figure.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Coach Tolkachev, Burevestnik sports school, Soviet gymnastics system, exceptional physical qualities, late start at 11
evidence_summary: Andrianov entered gymnastics relatively late at age 11 but was fortunate to be spotted by renowned Soviet coach Nikolai Tolkachev, who became his surrogate father and provided sustained, individualized training. The Soviet gymnastics pipeline — from the Burevestnik sports school to the national team — concentrated elite training and competition access. Andrianov possessed exceptional upper body strength combined with phenomenal suppleness, enabling rapid progress. He was selected for the USSR national team at 18 and won his first European Championship golds at 19. Raised by a single mother in Vladimir, his family financial background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Vladimir, Russian SFSR; raised by his mother; entered gymnastics at age 11 at the Burevestnik sports school.
current_position: Died on March 21, 2011 in Vladimir, Russia at age 58; final role: head coach of Soviet national men's junior gymnastics team (1981-1992).

name: Walter Browne
milestone_by_age_26: Awarded the Grandmaster title by FIDE in 1970 at age 21, becoming the first GM born after World War II and the youngest GM in the world at the time.
early_history_summary: Born in Sydney, Australia to an American father (export-import business) and Australian mother, Browne moved to Brooklyn, New York at age 3. His father taught him chess at 8. He joined the Manhattan Chess Club at 13, playing or studying chess every day for a full year. He won the U.S. Junior Championship in 1966 at 17, the Australian Chess Championship in 1969 at 20, and earned the Grandmaster title at the San Juan tournament in 1970 by tying for 2nd-4th behind world champion Boris Spassky.
family_context_summary: Born in Sydney, Australia to an American father in the export-import business and an Australian mother; moved to Brooklyn, New York at age 3; father taught him chess at age 8.

evidence_summary: Browne benefited from early chess instruction by his father at age 8 and access to the Manhattan Chess Club at 13, one of the world's most prestigious chess institutions. Growing up in Brooklyn during the Fischer era placed him at the center of American chess. He showed exceptional dedication, playing or studying chess every day for a full year as a teenager. His father's export-import business provided the financial means for the family's move from Australia to New York. He won the U.S. Junior Championship at 17, the Australian Championship at 20, and became the world's youngest Grandmaster at 21 in 1970.
